title: The Richest Man in Babylon
author: George S. Clason
blurb: First published in 1926 as a series of pamphlets, this book teaches personal finance through parables set in ancient Babylon. A chariot builder named Bansir realizes that after years of hard work he has nothing to show for it. He and his friend Kobbi seek out their childhood friend Arkad, now the richest man in the city. Arkad explains that wealth follows simple laws anyone can learn. Keep a part of everything you earn. Live below your income. Put your savings to work, and protect them by taking advice only from people who truly know their trade. Later stories carry these ideas further. A former slave named Dabasir climbs out of debt, and Arkad's son learns the Five Laws of Gold. The message is that steady habits, not luck, build lasting wealth.

lessons.t: Why Hard Work Alone Leaves You Broke
lessons.b: Bansir works hard for years and still has nothing, which shows that wealth comes from understanding the laws of money, not from labor or luck alone.

lessons.t: A Part of All You Earn
lessons.b: Arkad's first secret is to pay yourself first by keeping at least one tenth of everything you earn before spending anything.
Your so-called necessary expenses tend to grow to match your income, so you must budget deliberately to live on less than you make.
